disposition_reason: Table 1 prints annual mean Pb, Ni, Hg, Cu, Zn and Cd in Orel-region wheat grain (2015-2018); Table 2 prints Pb, Ni, Zn and Cu in grain after steeping with enzyme preparations, with and without washing.

controls.control: grain steeping with cellulolytic enzyme complex preparation A
grain steeping with enzyme preparation A followed by washing with running water
controls.outcome: Pb 0.187 (washed control) or 0.256 (unwashed control) -> 0.059 mg/kg; text states -68.4% Pb, -99% Ni (table shows Ni 0.101 vs control 0.254/0.119), -28.4% Zn, -14.1% Cu

controls.control: hemicellulase preparation B steeping plus washing

unresolved: Table 1 2018 Cu and Zn printed '-' (not determined); no finding recorded.
The plus-minus sign is missing from the text layer; second numbers read as dispersion of unstated type.
Text says Celloviridin-type steeping plus washing cut nickel by 99%, but Table 2 shows 0.101 vs 0.254 mg/kg (about -60%).
Per-year sample counts and the Table 1 analytical method are not stated; heavy metals by HPLC peak area is unconventional and unvalidated here.
Text says some grain exceeded permissible levels for Pb, Ni and Hg, without counts.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Customs Union technical regulation TR CU 021/2011 'On Food Safety' permissible levels referenced
